panels.title: 1 — Poller stopped
panels.description:
critical · fires above 900 for 5m

No poller tick for 15 minutes. The tick moves every ~60 s regardless of upstream, so this is the thread or the pod rather than a quiet night, and /health's self-healing did not recover it. Check the pod; a restart is the usual response.

panels.title: 1a — No poller leader
panels.description:
critical · fires below 1 for 5m

No API pod has led for 5 minutes: no rebuild cycle, no push, no webhook emit, no labelling check. The pods still serve the last-built tables, so reads look healthy while refreshed_at ages. Expected and self-clearing after a SIGKILLed or crashed leader: the successor waits out the 300 s lease TTL plus one 60 s tick, which is longer than this rule's pending window, so a forced kill fires it once. Otherwise look at event="poller_lease" records in ent-kub-<env> namespace kix-avvik (acquire_failed and error mean the Firestore notifications database is failing; refused means some holder's held_until is still in the future) and at /ready's role on each pod. Never delete the lease document. Runbook: docs/operations/poller-lease.md.

panels.title: 1b — Two poller leaders
panels.description:
critical · fires above 1 for 1m

Two pods have each reported leading for over a minute. The gauge is each pod's own belief, so this is two pods that BOTH think they lead, which a stalled leader does until its next boundary or tick: tolerated for less than the pending minute during a handoff after a stall, and a firing is not. Both may be rebuilding the same tables and pushing the same alerts. Check event="poller_lease" (acquired on one pod, lost or lease_lost on the other) and the duplicate check over event="push" result="sent" per journey and situation. If it persists, delete the stalled pod — the one whose own series reads 1 while its /ready answers role follower (its local deadline has passed; only the gauge has not caught up) — never the lease document. Runbook: docs/operations/poller-lease.md.

panels.title: 2 — Rebuild stale
panels.description:
warning · fires above 3600 for 15m

Cycle freshness, not liveness: cycles are event-driven and pause legitimately on quiet nights. If rules 1 and 1a are silent a pod is alive and leads — look at poller_phase errors and at whether the SIRI-SX ingestion timestamp is moving.

panels.title: 2a — Subscription mirror stale
panels.description:
warning · fires above 900 for 15m

The webhook pass is matching an old subscription population: a revoked recipient keeps getting alerts and a new one gets none. Look at poller_phase records with phase=notification_mirror and result=error. A sync that keeps truncating at its page budget also grows this: check truncated on the mirror_sync records before treating it as a failure. Past 6 h the store re-seeds itself; past ~24 h revocations are lost for good.

panels.title: 2b — Worker stopped
panels.description:
critical · fires above 900 for 5m

No delivery round for 15 minutes; the tick moves on every round, including the ones that find nothing. Check the kix-avvik-worker Deployment — scaled to zero, rolled back, or crash-looping. Pending webhook events expire after an hour.

panels.title: 2c — Delivery backlog
panels.description:
warning · fires above 1800 for 15m

The oldest deliverable pending delivery was minted over 30 min ago, and an event is valid for 60. Response: raise deployment.forceReplicas in helm/kix-avvik/env/worker-values-kub-ent-<env>.yaml — the drain formula is in docs/operations/notification-webhooks.md.

panels.title: 3 — Pod restarts
panels.description:
warning · fires above 3 for 0m

More than 3 restarts in 15 minutes. A flapping /health lands here; the crash-loop escape is HEALTH_STALE_AFTER_S=0 through a values-only deploy, which disables the staleness branch.

panels.title: 4 — Memory near limit
panels.description:
critical · fires above 0.85 for 5m

Working set above 85 % of the container's limit. Since common 2.x the limit EQUALS the request, so the response is raising memory: in that release's values file. An OOM kill of an API pod at the autoscaler's minimum of one (and always in tst) is a full outage; at two or three it costs that pod's share of traffic, and if it was the leader, a handoff that waits out the 300 s lease TTL.

targets.expr:
sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="kix-avvik", container!="", prometheus_group="$env"})
/
sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{exported_namespace="kix-avvik", resource="memory", prometheus_group="$env"})

panels.title: 5 — Pod not ready
panels.description:
critical · fires below 1 for 3m

At one API pod (the autoscaler's minimum, and always in tst) not-ready means the service is down; at two or three it means one pod is out of rotation. In dev and prd readiness is /ready, which is 503 until the pod's prediction cache and timetable spine have loaded (reason predictions_not_loaded or plan_not_loaded in the body); in tst it is /health, whose dead-or-stale-poller 503s land here. Check the pod's events and logs.

panels.title: 6 — ERROR logged
panels.description:
warning · fires above 0 for 0m

The ERROR channel is deliberately near-silent, so any ERROR is worth a look. labelling_stale, thread_died and health_degraded all arrive here. Read the record in Cloud Logging — cluster project ent-kub-dev, namespace kix-avvik, not the app project.

panels.title: 7 — Push failures
panels.description:
warning · fires above 0.2 for 10m

More than 20 % of push attempts failed over 30 minutes, across at least 5 attempts. gone is not an error — that is a device that unsubscribed. Check smart_avvik_push_total by result and the varsel push logs.

targets.expr:
sum(increase(smart_avvik_push_total{result="error", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m]))
/
sum(increase(smart_avvik_push_total{kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m]))
and on()
sum(increase(smart_avvik_push_total{kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m])) > 5

panels.title: 8 — LLM wording failures
panels.description:
warning · fires above 0.3 for 10m

Over 30 % of live wording attempts failed in 30 minutes. Travellers still receive the deterministic template, so this is quality degradation rather than an outage. Check jsonPayload.event="llm_message" for provider and result; VARSEL_LLM_PROVIDER=off is the egress kill switch and VARSEL_LLM_ENABLED=false the bad-text revert.

targets.expr:
sum(increase(smart_avvik_llm_message_total{surface="live", result=~"error|unavailable|truncated|rejected", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m]))
/
sum(increase(smart_avvik_llm_message_total{surface="live", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m]))
and on()
sum(increase(smart_avvik_llm_message_total{surface="live", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m])) > 5

sum(increase(smart_avvik_llm_message_total{surface="live", result=~"error|unavailable|truncated|rejected", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m]))
/
sum(increase(smart_avvik_llm_message_total{surface="live", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[30m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: 8b — LLM replies rejected
panels.description:
warning · fires above 2 for 0m

More than two live wordings in an hour were thrown away as unusable. The traveller got the deterministic template. Read jsonPayload.reason on event="llm_message" result="rejected": too_long (with chars) means the reply broke the 300-character cap, usually after a prompt or train-label change; empty or malformed points at the backend. VARSEL_LLM_ENABLED=false is the bad-text revert.

panels.title: 9 — Labelling stale
panels.description:
critical · fires above 172800 for 30m

48 hours without successful labelling while decisions were still being written. Unlabelled decisions become permanently unknown after 10 days. Check the varsel-label-daily scheduled query in this environment's project.

panels.title: 10 — 5xx rate
panels.description:
critical · fires above 0.05 for 5m

5xx rate above 5 % for 5 minutes, excluding /health. Check the access log and rule 1 — a wedged poller shows up on both.

targets.expr:
sum(rate(smart_avvik_http_requests_total{status="5xx", path!="health", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[5m]))
/
sum(rate(smart_avvik_http_requests_total{path!="health", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: 11 — p99 latency
panels.description:
warning · fires above 5 for 10m

Golden-path default threshold, not yet tuned against this app's real traffic. Check whether one path dominates before treating it as a regression.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(smart_avvik_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{path!="health", long_poll!="true", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[5m])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(smart_avvik_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{path!="health", long_poll!="true", kubernetes_namespace="kix-avvik", prometheus_group="$env"}[5m]))) or vector(0)
